nameStory: The smooth green snake gets its name from two key features that make it unmistakable: its brilliant emerald-green color and its perfectly smooth scales. Unlike its cousin the rough green snake, this little serpent's scales lie flat and feel silky to the touch, earning it the 'smooth' part of its name.
description: The smooth green snake is a slender, gentle serpent that looks like a living piece of bright green grass. Adults typically measure 14-20 inches long, making them one of New England's smaller snakes. Their entire body is covered in brilliant emerald-green scales that help them disappear among vegetation. These non-venomous snakes are so docile they rarely bite, preferring to flee or freeze when discovered.

idTips.label: Pattern
idTips.description: Solid bright emerald-green coloration from head to tail with no patterns, stripes, or markings - like a living blade of grass

idTips.label: Scales
idTips.description: Scales feel completely smooth and silky when touched, lying flat against the body without any ridges or keels

idTips.label: Size
idTips.description: Small and slender, typically 14-20 inches long - about the length of a ruler - with a pencil-thin body

idTips.label: Head Shape
idTips.description: Small, narrow head that's barely wider than the neck, with round pupils and a pointed snout

idTips.label: Behavior
idTips.description: Often bobs its head slowly to mimic grass or small plants swaying in the breeze when trying to hide

habitat: Look for smooth green snakes in sunny, grassy areas like meadows, marshes, and woodland edges where they hunt insects. They love areas near streams and ponds where the grass stays lush and green. You might also spot them in open woodlands with grassy understory or along the weedy margins of wetlands.

seasonality.spring: Emerges from winter hiding spots in late spring and begins mating season. Look for them basking in sunny grass patches on warm days.
seasonality.summer: Most active period for hunting insects in tall grass and vegetation. Females lay eggs from June through early summer.
seasonality.fall: Continues hunting until temperatures drop, preparing for winter by feeding heavily on remaining insects before seeking shelter.
seasonality.winter: Hibernates underground in rock crevices, old rodent burrows, or beneath deep leaf litter and logs.

funFact: When a smooth green snake dies, its brilliant emerald color quickly fades to dull blue or gray within hours, which is why museum specimens never show their true living beauty.
confusionNotes: Most commonly confused with the rough green snake, but the rough green snake has keeled (ridged) scales that feel bumpy, while smooth green snakes have perfectly flat, silky scales. Remember: if it feels smooth, it's a smooth green snake!
contextualKnowledge: This species is sometimes called a 'grass snake,' but this name can be confusing since several other snake species share this common name. Always use 'smooth green snake' to avoid mix-ups with other species.
compareHints: The smooth green snake is the only member of the green snake genus found in New England, making identification easier. When compared to other small, solid-colored snakes in the region like brown snakes or red-bellied snakes, the smooth green snake's bright emerald color is unmistakable. No other New England snake shares this vibrant grass-green coloration.
